title: AMD stock jumps 13% after 5-star analyst resets price target
detail:
AMD stock jumps 13% after 5-star analyst resets price target
Mwangi Enos
Tue, November 10, 2026 at 2:07 PM MST 4 min read
AMD
Trade AMD on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

I work on my computer, switching between research, market data, writing, and my trading platforms. I notice when applications respond quickly and when my machine struggles to keep up with several tasks at once. A frustrating issue I had with my previous six-year-old laptop. 

It honestly made me appreciate how much the processor matters, even when I rarely think about the chip powering it.

AMD makes chips for devices like those, but its fortunes now hinge on data centers. In the third quarter, data center revenue hit a record $8.5 billion, up 97%, while client chip revenue rose 7% to $2.9 billion and gaming fell 40% to $773 million.

AMD CEO Lisa Su called it "a record quarter with revenue exceeding the high end of our guidance" and said growth should accelerate as Helios and Venice ramp. AMD guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $17 billion, up 66%, and management expects more than 80% growth next year despite supply limits.

Also Read: AMD's biggest AI deals come with a 320 million share catch

AMD jumps 13% as an upgrade tests the pullback

On Nov. 9, AMD closed at $508.58, up 13.26%, after Oppenheimer analyst Rick Schafer upgraded it from Perform to Outperform with a $600 price target, about 18% higher, in a note shared with TheStreet. 

TipRanks ranks Schafer No. 20 of 12,555 analysts it tracks, with a 70% success rate and a 30.50% average return per rating.

AMD's strong performance is reflected in its shares, still up 137.48% this year and 117.77% over one year, according to Yahoo Finance, even after the pullback that began following earnings on Nov. 3.

AMD also said its fifth-generation EPYC processors power Google Cloud's TPU 8tx, adding hardware-enforced confidential computing for that cloud's AI systems.

Why Oppenheimer turned bullish

Oppenheimer raised estimates after speaking with CFO Jean Hu and investor relations head Matt Ramsay. It expects data center revenue to grow 135% in 2027 and reach 85% of total sales, as GPU sales overtake server CPU revenue. It models about 3 gigawatts of computing capacity shipped in 2027 and 4 gigawatts in 2028.

The customers are household names in AI.

OpenAI and Meta should drive data center sales through the first quarter. Anthropic could ramp late in that quarter, and Oracle, Microsoft and Humain may support growth through 2028. Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle already run workloads on AMD's first Helios rack-scale systems.

Oppenheimer upgraded Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) stock to Outperform from Perform on Monday and set a $600 price target, citing data center momentum, according to a research note.

Data center revenue about doubled in the third quarter, supported by EPYC server processor sales and early shipments of MI455 AI chips and Helios server racks, analyst Rick Schafer said.

The analyst played down worries that midterm elections could slow data center construction, saying many planned projects are already in progress. The five largest cloud providers are expected to spend about $1.3 trillion on capital projects in 2027, compared with $800 billion this year.

AI graphics chip sales are expected to overtake server CPU sales in 2027, Schafer said, even as server CPU revenue more than doubles.

Nvidia's 70% to 80% Margins Are "Like Throwing Chum in the Water," Says Its Biographer ©Nana Dua from Pexels and Изображения пользователя Valeriya Luzina via Canva
Key Takeaways

Nvidia fell 4% on Monday after its board opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang.

Nvidia's 71% gross margin gives its biggest buyers every reason to back cheaper chips, and Anthropic training its AI almost entirely on chips Google designs shows how that can work.

Analysts still expect Nvidia's revenue to more than triple from fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2028, so the pressure is likelier to show up in its margin before its sales.

Nvidia's Nov. 17 report is the next test, with management already guiding gross margin down to 71% to 72% in the January quarter as memory costs climb.

Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) fell 4% on Monday after its board opened an independent investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

The rest of the chip trade went the other way. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD:NASDAQ) jumped 13%, helped by a new collaboration with Google Cloud, and Broadcom (AVGO:NASDAQ) rose 9%.

Stephen Witt, whose book The Thinking Machine tells the story of Huang and Nvidia, was asked on Monday's Squawk Pod whether Nvidia's competitors were feeling some glee. His answer came down to price. Nvidia's margins, he said, "are 70, 80%. I mean, that's the kind of margin, that's like throwing chum in the water."

And the sharks have already had a taste. Anthropic, expected to go public later this month, trained its AI "almost completely on Google's TPU stack," Witt said. Those are the custom chips Alphabet (GOOG) designs with Broadcom.

So it's no surprise that Witt told this week's Hard Fork podcast that what's bad for Nvidia is good for AMD, Broadcom and Google.

The orders are still there

Anthropic is one customer. Witt himself agreed that Anthropic runs its models on Nvidia chips it rents, and he said the inference market "still kind of favors NVIDIA." Wall Street also sees Nvidia's revenue more than tripling between the year ended January 2026 and fiscal 2028:

Nvidia (NVDA): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2025-2029 (years to January) (TIKR)

That's $215.9 billion growing to $692 billion. When it reported in August, management guided to about 70% growth in fiscal 2028 and said supply was what held it there. A board investigation doesn't change how many chips Nvidia can get made, so I don't expect Monday's news to move those estimates.

Cerebras Systems CBRS is set to release its third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 12.

For the third quarter of 2026, Cerebras expects core revenues to be in the range of $214-$216 million.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for revenues is pegged at $215.82 million. Cerebras reported revenues of $209.87 million in the second quarter of 2026.

The consensus mark for loss has been steady at 13 cents per share over the past 30 days. Cerebras reported a loss of 4 cents per share in the second quarter of 2026, narrower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate, delivering an 80.95% earnings surprise.

Cerebras Systems Inc. Price and EPS Surprise
Cerebras Systems Inc. Price and EPS Surprise

Cerebras Systems Inc. price-eps-surprise | Cerebras Systems Inc. Quote

Let's see how things are shaping up prior to this announcement.

Key Factors to Note for Cerebras' Q3 Earnings

Cerebras Systems' third-quarter 2026 performance is expected to have benefited from robust demand for high-speed AI inference, expanding cloud deployments and growing adoption of its wafer-scale computing technology. Increasing demand for faster token generation across AI coding, agentic workflows and enterprise applications is likely to have supported revenue growth.

The continued ramp-up of Cerebras Systems deployment with OpenAI is expected to be a major growth driver in the to-be-reported quarter. The company's ability to serve advanced frontier models, including GPT-5.6 Sol, at significantly higher inference speeds strengthens its competitive positioning. Growing usage among existing cloud customers is also likely to have boosted cloud and services revenues. In the second quarter of 2026, core cloud and other services revenues surged 287% year over year to $127.7 million, reflecting strong demand for its inference offerings.

Expanding enterprise adoption is another positive factor. Cerebras Systems secured agreements with Figma, Cognition and Lovable in AI coding, while Block, AlphaSense and GSK adopted its technology for agentic applications. Its engagement with CrowdStrike also highlights emerging opportunities in AI-powered cybersecurity. These customer additions are expected to have supported cloud utilization and broaden the company's revenue base in the to-be-reported quarter.

However, the company is expected to have suffered from rising infrastructure investments and near-term margin pressure associated with its aggressive capacity expansion. In the second quarter of 2026, core gross margin declined 590 basis points (bps) sequentially to 40.6% as Cerebras Systems temporarily rented systems back from customers to satisfy strong inference demand.

The company expects the third quarter of 2026 to represent the trough, with core gross margin guided to 38-40%, while core operating margin is expected to deteriorate to negative 25-23% from negative 16% in the second quarter of 2026. Continued investments in manufacturing, data centers, research and development and organizational infrastructure are also likely to have weighed on operating profitability. Management projects a core operating margin between negative 25% and negative 23% in the third quarter of 2026 compared with negative 16% in the second quarter.

title: Google, Nvidia and Microsoft “Literally Feeding Themselves Money” with $26 Billion Anthropic IPO Buy

Google, Nvidia and Microsoft “Literally Feeding Themselves Money” with $26 Billion Anthropic IPO Buy

Google, Nvidia and Microsoft "Literally Feeding Themselves Money" with $26 Billion Anthropic IPO Buy ©Natee Meepian's Images and Nana Dua from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Alphabet's Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, Broadcom, AMD, Micron and TSMC will buy $26 billion of Anthropic's shares at its IPO price, on top of an offering of up to $64.4 billion.

Most of those buyers also sell Anthropic the computing behind its $895 billion of commitments, so part of the cash that pays their bills is their own.

Broadcom has the most at stake, with $161 billion of Anthropic's commitments against $63.9 billion of revenue in fiscal 2025.

The buyers face no six-month lockup, and the Anthropic share of their backlogs is only as solid as Anthropic's next few quarters.

Google parent Alphabet (GOOG) is about to buy into one of its biggest customers, and it's bringing company.

Alphabet, Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ), Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ), Broadcom (AVGO:NASDAQ), AMD, Micron and TSMC will buy $26 billion of Anthropic's shares at its IPO price through a private placement, Anthropic's updated filing on Tuesday shows. That's on top of the up to $64.4 billion Anthropic and some of its backers are raising in the IPO itself, at $70 to $78 a share.

Tech critic Ed Zitron wasn't impressed. When word of the deal broke on Monday, he posted on X that "shareholders should revolt," since the buyers are "literally feeding themselves money."

Harsh, but he has a point.

Follow the money

Anthropic's filing shows $895 billion of commitments, mostly for computing power and chips, and about $70 billion of that comes due in the year through September 2027. Its S-1 puts the biggest pieces with Broadcom, at $161 billion, and Google, at $121 billion. Microsoft, like Google, is both an Anthropic backer and a key supplier of its computing power.

So the companies sending Anthropic its bills are now covering part of them. The $26 billion works out to more than a third of what Anthropic owes over the next year.

Nor is this the first loop. In November 2025, Nvidia agreed to invest up to $10 billion in Anthropic and Microsoft up to $5 billion, while Anthropic committed to buy $30 billion of computing on Microsoft's Azure cloud and up to a gigawatt of capacity on Nvidia's systems.
